source.howDecided: In src/caldiy: `git log --format='%h %ad %s' --date=short 038381aeca..origin/main -- <culprit files>` returned nothing. The whole delta 038381aeca..176037d0af is 4 commits (#29819 Clara app, #29740 phone-input country fallback, #29901 language update, #29940 customReplyToEmail) and `git diff --stat 038381aeca origin/main` lists 16 files, none of them a culprit file for this finding. I then read the culprit region out of today's head with `git show origin/main:<file>` and re-numbered it: the lines are byte-identical to the tested tree and sit at the same line numbers. addAttendee at today's head is identical: it loads the booking with getByUidWithEventType (line 76), throws only NotFoundException when the booking is missing (lines 77-79), and delegates straight to this.bookingAttendeesService.addAttendee (line 87) with no read of eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot anywhere. The shared service is at packages/features/bookings/services/BookingAttendeesService.ts (the FINDINGS-INDEX path packages/features/bookings/lib/BookingAttendeesService.ts does not exist at head; the review's path is the right one), and it is untouched too.

citedItems.note: The PR that introduced the endpoint without a seats guard (the review's introducedBy). Last updated 2026-02-17, no activity since. Not a report of the bug.

queries: gh search issues --owner calcom --include-prs --limit 30 --updated '>2026-08-01' 'seated seats'  (0 results)
gh search issues --owner calcom --include-prs --limit 30 '"does not support seated"'  (0 results, i.e. the documented refusal sentence appears in no issue or PR title/body anywhere in the org)

reevaluation: Stands unchanged. Neither booking-attendees.service.ts (v2), packages/features/bookings/services/BookingAttendeesService.ts nor booking-guests.service.ts was touched by any of the 4 commits since the tested tree, so POST /v2/bookings/{uid}/attendees on a seated booking still returns 201 and still creates an Attendee row with no BookingSeat. No new tracker item: nothing seated-related has been updated org-wide since 2026-08-01 and the documented refusal sentence appears nowhere in the tracker. The review's cited PR #27759 is unchanged (merged 2026-02-17). One framing point survives re-check and must be in the filed issue: the promise "Attempting to add an attendee to a seated event booking will return a 400 error" exists only in cal.com's published OpenAPI; the Cal.diy controller's own @ApiOperation has no Seated Events paragraph, so this is most likely a guard added on the commercial side after the April 2026 fork and never ported. That does not make it an edition mismatch, because the harm (a seat-less attendee that violates Cal.diy's own required seatUid in GetSeatedBookingOutput and splits its two seat counters) is entirely inside Cal.diy code.
policyBasis: calcom/cal.diy .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml sets `blank_issues_enabled: false`, so a bug must go through bug_report.md (Issue Summary / Steps to Reproduce / Actual Results / Expected Results / Technical details / Evidence, the last called "quite mandatory in terms of bugs"); CONTRIBUTING.md: "For bugs, security, performance, documentation, etc., you can start coding immediately, even if the `needs approval` label is present", so no discussion-first gate applies.
notes: Only the first half of the finding is evidenced by the run: the add is accepted (201, attendee id 79 on booking 73, event type 102 with seatsPerTimeSlot 10). The seat-count drift (display counts raw Attendee rows, the seat gate counts only rows with a BookingSeat) is derived from source, not observed, because the scenario aborted at step 2 and nothing re-read the booking. The FINDINGS-INDEX liveNote asks for exactly that re-read; until it is done the issue should claim the 201 and describe the seat arithmetic as a code-level consequence. The guests endpoint (booking-guests.service.ts) has the identical hole and its documented refusal is equally false, so file both in one issue. calcom/cal.com and calcom/cal.diy are the SAME repository: gh api repos/calcom/cal.com returns full_name calcom/cal.diy (the repo was renamed, GitHub redirects the old path). Every calcom/cal.com#NNNN reference in the review resolves to the same number on calcom/cal.diy, and one `--owner calcom` search covers both. The commercial Cal.com source is private, so nothing about the hosted product is verifiable and no "fixed in cal.com" claim can be made.
